title: Clarity of Scripture
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The clarity of Scripture means that God has spoken in a way His people can truly understand, believe, and obey. Though some passages are difficult, Scripture is not a closed book reserved only for experts.
summary: The clarity of Scripture means that God has spoken in a way His people can truly understand, believe, and obey. Though some passages are difficult, Scripture is not a closed book reserved only for experts.
christFocus: Jesus taught from Scripture in ways that called ordinary people to hear, understand, repent, and follow Him. The clear message of Scripture leads sinners to Christ and teaches believers to walk in His ways.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s Word is a lamp and light for His people. Scripture is not meant to hide God’s will from those who humbly seek Him. God speaks so that His people may know Him, trust Him, and obey Him.

The clarity of Scripture does not mean every verse is equally simple or that careful study is unnecessary. Some things require patience, teaching, context, and maturity. But the central truths of Scripture—God, sin, salvation, Christ, faith, repentance, obedience, and hope—are given clearly enough to be understood.

This doctrine encourages ordinary believers. Children, new believers, the poor, the suffering, the disabled, the recovering, and those without formal education are not excluded from receiving God’s Word. The Bible is for the people of God, not merely for religious elites.

Faithful teachers help make the sense clear, as seen when the Word was read and explained to the people. Teaching does not replace Scripture’s clarity; it serves it by helping people understand what God has spoken.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people feel intimidated by the Bible and assume they can never understand it. Others have been made dependent on leaders who act as though only they can truly interpret God’s Word. The clarity of Scripture pushes back against both despair and control.

This doctrine invites believers to come to Scripture with humility and hope. God has not mocked His people by giving them a Word they cannot receive. He gives light, wisdom, warning, and instruction through what He has written.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read Scripture with humility, prayer, and expectation. Do not let difficulty keep you from what is clear. Begin with the plain message of the text, seek faithful teaching when needed, and obey what God makes known. Trust that the Lord speaks through His Word to ordinary people who come to Him in faith.
